question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: It was long after midnight when we locked up the Englishman and went to bed ourselves.

A. Noble took it very quietly.

B. I having thought of the same thing myself (among many others) said no, because it was more than likely the English wouldn’t shoot our men.

C. As I blew out the candle I told Noble what Jeremiah Donovan had told me.

D. After we had been in bed about an hour he asked me did I think we ought to tell the Englishmen.

S2: “I think so,” says Noble.
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, A, D, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A chronological bedtime conversation between the narrator and Noble.

• C (continues the immediate bedtime action of S1, telling Noble what he had learned) → A (‘it’ refers to what was told to Noble in C) → D (‘After’ places this later, continuing from the quiet reaction in A) → B (the direct reply to the question just asked in D)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A question must be followed by the answer to that specific question.

 

NOTE

• B is the narrator's answer to the question posed in D, so B cannot precede D.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Then the Spring came, and all over the country there were little blossoms and little birds.

A. The only people who were pleased were the Snow and the Frost.

B. Only in the garden of the Selfish Giant it was still winter.

C. The birds did not care to sing in it as there were no children, and the trees forgot to blossom.

D. Once a beautiful flower put its head out from the grass, but when it saw the notice-board it was so sorry for the children that it slipped back into the ground again and went off to sleep.

S2: “Spring has forgotten this garden,” they cried, “so we will live here all the year round.”
solution_text:
The correct answer is B, C, D, A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A contrast (spring everywhere except one garden), then its description and summary.

• B (‘Only’ contrasts the general spring of S1 with one exceptional garden) → C (continues describing that garden (‘it’/‘there’) from B) → D (a specific incident illustrating the garden's wintry state described in C) → A (sums up who benefited from the wintry garden just described)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘Only’ signals an exception that must be introduced before its details are elaborated.

 

NOTE

• C, D and A all describe the exceptional garden named in B, so B must come first.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: So why develop your financial genius?

A. I can tell you why I have been developing this area of my intelligence.

B. Not because I need to, but because I want to.

C. Only you can answer that.

D. I do it because I want to make money fast.

S2: It is a fascinating learning process.
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, A, D, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A question, an acknowledgement, then the narrator's reasoned explanation.

• C (the direct reply to the question posed in S1) → A (the narrator's own answer, following on from ‘answer that’ in C) → D (gives the specific reason, continuing A's explanation) → B (clarifies and refines the reason just given in D)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A ‘not because X, but because Y’ clarification always follows the reason it is refining.

 

NOTE

• B directly qualifies the reason given in D, so it cannot precede D.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Sofia stood listening to the noise of the departing carriage which bore away her mother and sister.

A. As a child, when some wrong or injustice had been done her, she had cried all alone, when she was in bed, in the dark, and the habit had remained with her.

B. She was left alone, quite alone, as she had always wished to be left.

C. Certainly in these moments of complete solitude the consciousness of a great grief came over her.

D. Now, alone in the great drawing room, beneath the brightly lighted chandelier, her hands inert, her head resting against the back of her chair, her face wore an expression of great sorrow.

S2: The sentiment of the reality, long repulsed, became clear, distinct, and cruel.
solution_text:
The correct answer is B, A, D, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Present solitude, a childhood memory, then a return to the present grief.

• B (the direct consequence of the family's departure described in S1) → A (recalls a childhood pattern of being alone, following B's statement of being ‘left alone’) → D (‘Now’ returns to the present scene, contrasting with the childhood memory in A) → C (continues the present emotional description from D)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘Now’ typically signals a return to the present after a flashback.

 

NOTE

• D's ‘Now’ only makes sense after the childhood recollection in A, so A must precede D.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: The next morning I went to see her, but when I entered the hut, she, poor thing, was already stark and cold.

A. They were good folk.

B. The babies were left alone.

C. In dying, she had rolled on to this child and crushed her leg.

D. The village folk came to the hut, washed the body, laid her out, made a coffin, and buried her.

S2: What was to be done with them?
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, D, A, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The cause of death, the community's response, and its consequence.

• C (explains the scene of death from S1 in more detail) → D (the community's response following the death described in C) → A (comments on the village folk just introduced in D) → B (describes the resulting situation after the burial in D)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A short evaluative sentence like ‘They were good folk’ usually follows right after the people it describes are introduced.

 

NOTE

• A's ‘They’ needs ‘the village folk’ from D already named, so D precedes A.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: One day in autumn on my way back from a remote part of the country I caught cold and fell ill.

A. He prescribed me the usual sudorific, ordered a mustard plaster to be put on, very deftly slid a five-ruble note up his sleeve, coughing drily and looking away as he did so, and then getting up to go home, but somehow fell into talk and remained.

B. I was exhausted with feverishness; I foresaw a sleepless night and was glad of a little chat with a pleasant companion.

C. Fortunately, the fever attacked me in the district town at the inn; I sent for the doctor.

D. In half an hour the district doctor appeared, a thin, dark- haired man of middle height.

S2: Tea was served.
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, D, A, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chronological illness, the doctor's arrival, treatment, and reflection.

• C (direct continuation of falling ill in S1, sending for the doctor) → D (the direct result of sending for the doctor in C) → A (describes what the doctor, just introduced in D, did) → B (the narrator's own reflection, leading into S2's ‘Tea was served’)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• An action by a person must follow that person's introduction.

 

NOTE

• A's ‘He’ refers to the doctor introduced only in D, so D must precede A.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: For the first time it occurred to me that if things worked out the way everyone was hoping, I’d be going halfway around the world to live with a man I hadn’t even met.

A. It would be ungrateful.

B. Don’t send me so far away, I wanted to cry, but of course I didn’t.

C. Would I ever see my parents again?

D. Father had worked so hard to find this match for me.

S2: Besides, wasn’t it every woman’s destiny, as Mother was always telling me, to leave the known for the unknown?
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, B, A, D.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An emotional reaction and self-restraint, then the reason for that restraint.

• C (the narrator's immediate worried thought following S1) → B (continues the emotional reaction from C) → A (‘It’ refers to crying out, explaining why she ‘didn't’ in B) → D (gives the reason it would be ungrateful, continuing from A)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A short evaluative sentence built on ‘It’ usually explains the action just mentioned before it.

 

NOTE

• A only makes sense right after B's ‘I wanted to cry, but... didn't,’ and D explains why, so D follows A.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: I was an outsider, and as I had no special matters to air, I was able to spend the evening independently of the others.

A. He was tall, rather thin, very serious, and well dressed.

B. He was the first to attract my attention.

C. There was another gentleman present who like myself had just stumbled upon this affair of domestic bliss.

D. His appearance was not that of a man of birth or high family.

S2: Apparently he had no heart for the family festivities.
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, B, D, A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Introduction of a character, followed by his physical description.

• C (introduces the other gentleman present) → B (‘He’ refers to the gentleman just introduced in C) → D (continues describing ‘his’ appearance) → A (further physical description, following D)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• A person must be introduced before pronouns describing him are used.

 

NOTE

• B, D and A all use ‘He/His’ referring to the gentleman named only in C, so C must come first.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Sofia did not raise her eyes from her work, and her slim fingers fairly flew over the delicate lace.

A. She hummed a few bars of a song and recited a verse, but Sofia appeared not to hear.

B. But Lulu wandered about the room, moving the ornaments on the shelves or opening a drawer to gaze absently into it.

C. Then Lulu, who was not blessed with too much patience, decided to put the question boldly, and planting herself in front of her sister, she asked:

D. It was clear that she wished either to do or to say something but was abashed by her elder sister’s grave manner.

S2: “Sofia, do you know what Mademoiselle Jeannette told me?”
solution_text:
The correct answer is B, D, A, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lulu's growing restlessness, leading to her finally speaking.

• B (‘But’ contrasts Lulu's restlessness with Sofia's focus in S1) → D (‘she’ is Lulu, continuing from B, hesitant to speak) → A (Lulu's attempt to get attention, following her hesitation in D) → C (‘Then’ marks the decisive step after the earlier hesitant attempts)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• ‘Then’ often marks the final, decisive action after a build-up of smaller attempts.

 

NOTE

• C's decisive action must come after the earlier hesitant attempts described in D and A.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: He remained a day in order to earn the art, because he thought he might be able to turn it to use later on, if by chance he should fail to find other work in Batavia.

A. Neither on the first nor the second day had he realized how lonely he was, because he was captivated by the grand idea of earning enough money to buy two buffaloes.

B. The following day toward evening he thanked his host and departed.

C. He had left her in anxious hope.

D. As soon as it was dark, and no one could see him, he took out the Melati leaves Adinda had given him.

S2: The prospect of seeing her again so occupied his heart that on leaving Badoer and passing the tree, he felt something akin to joy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is B, D, A, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A chronological departure and journey, then reflection on leaving Adinda.

• B (‘The following day’ continues chronologically from the day mentioned in S1) → D (continues immediately after departing in B, now travelling by night) → A (reflects back over the first two days of travel begun in B and D) → C (a summarising reflection on leaving Adinda, leading into S2)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Time markers like ‘the following day’ and ‘as soon as it was dark’ fix the sequence of travel events.

 

NOTE

• A's reflection on ‘the first nor the second day’ only makes sense once the journey has begun in B and D.
